subject: Intermittent RPC failures during private cutover — SNAT sticky mapping & packet reordering
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicahealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Incident] RPC failures after private deployment cutover

Hi team,

We rolled the private deployment cutover in our staging VPC ~14:30 PDT and started seeing intermittent RPC failures from our backend services to the Redwood connectors. Symptoms: 10-15% of RPCs time out or return connection reset; retries succeed. App logs show lots of "TCP RST" and some "out of order" packet warnings.

Quick notes:
- Problem window: ~14:40–15:05 PDT.
- Affected endpoints: svc-store (backend) talking to redwood connector cluster in our VPC (10.40.0.0/22).
- We collected a short pcap and netflow summary (attached).

Can you advise immediate mitigations? We can roll back the cutover but we'd prefer a targeted fix if it's quick.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
NetOps Lead, MedicaHealth
attachments: medica_pcap_segment.pcap, netflow_report_may19.csv
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] RPC failures after private deployment cutover

Thanks for the quick report and the attachments, Samir — looking.

Initial hypothesis: two concurrent issues could explain the pattern:
1) SNAT port mapping instability or ephemeral-port exhaustion on the private gateway causing some backend connections to be remapped mid-flow (clients see RSTs / retries succeed).
2) Packet reordering/out-of-order segments between the connector and backend (we've seen TCP implementations silently drop heavily reordered sequences causing RPC level failures).

Immediate asks so we can triage faster:
- Short pcap of one failing RPC (you attached medica_pcap_segment.pcap — will start with that).
- Netflow CSV is helpful for port range usage.
- Can you confirm the gateway SNAT configuration (port range, conntrack timeout) and whether there is any ECMP in the path?

Short-term mitigations to consider (low-risk):
- Increase SNAT ephemeral port range on the gateway by +20000 ports, or enable port-preserving SNAT where possible.
- Increase conntrack timeouts for TCP_ESTABLISHED to 24h temporarily.
- If you can, enable TCP SACK and lower MSS/clamp to 1400 to reduce fragmentation and reordering impact.

I'll run the pcap and come back with packet-level notes. If it looks like a gateway bug we'll coordinate a narrow rollback window.

- Michael
Michael Grant
Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] RPC failures after private deployment cutover

I've looked through the pcap and pulled a short summary (attached as pcap_summary.txt). Key findings:
- Multiple flows show initial SYN, SYN-ACK, then a burst of out-of-order data segments arriving at the server; server responds with duplicate ACKs then RST in a subset of flows.
- The source IP seen by the backend for the same client 5-tuple flips mid-session on a few traces (same client port but different SNAT address), which strongly suggests SNAT mapping churn on the gateway.
- MTU mismatch: client-side MSS = 1448, path MTU variations seen where one hop is applying 1420 MSS clamp. We see fragmentation behavior in a few packets.

Interpretation: the most likely root cause is gateway SNAT behavior combined with transient path MTU/fragmentation that increases reordering/retransmit pressure. If the SNAT device moves a mapping (or hands off flows across devices) while packets are in flight, backend will see mismatched tuple and drop/close the connection.

Proposed immediate ops plan (low blast radius):
- On the gateway cluster: increase ephemeral port range and enable port-preserving SNAT on the affected pool (command examples below).
- Set conntrack tcp timeout to 86400 seconds for now.
- Apply MSS clamp to 1400 on the connector-facing interface to avoid fragmentation.
- Monitor RPC success rate for 30 minutes, then consider rolling the cutover forward.

Attachment: pcap_summary.txt (small summary + a few tcpdump snippets).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [Incident] RPC failures after private deployment cutover

Thanks — we've provisioned temporary captures for a 1-hour window and uploaded the full pcap to the Drive link (see ticket). Netflow shows high ephemeral port reuse on the gateway between 14:35–14:50. We also see many out-of-order segments (tcp.analysis.retransmission + tcp.analysis.out_of_order in Wireshark).

EdgeConnect (cc) — can you confirm whether your private gateway supports port-preserving SNAT on the pool we used for MedicaHealth? If not, can you temporarily allocate a dedicated SNAT IP for the connector cluster to avoid mapping collisions?

We are comfortable trying Marissa's ops plan in a short maintenance window (we can do 03:00–03:30 UTC tomorrow). If you have command snippets we can run in a ticket, paste them and we'll coordinate.

—Samir
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 03:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: [Incident] RPC failures after private deployment cutover — Proposed ops plan & commands

Forwarding the thread and proposing the exact change set for the maintenance window (03:00–03:30 UTC). Please review and ack or suggest tweaks. We'll coordinate with MedicaHealth and EdgeConnect.

Planned steps (order):
1) On gateway nodes (rolling per-AZ): increase ephemeral port range to include 32768-65535 -> append 20000 more ports (example sysctl/iptables snippet below).
   - iptables SNAT port-range example: --to-source 203.0.113.45:32768-98200 
2) Enable port-preserving SNAT where supported (EdgeConnect command: edgectl nat set-port-preserve true --pool-id 42). If edge does not support, request a dedicated SNAT IP for the pool.
3) Set conntrack tcp timeout: echo 86400 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established
4) Apply MSS clamp on connector-facing VTI: iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu --set-mss 1400
5) Re-run a small synthetic RPC test suite (we have the test harness link in the Jira) and watch packet drops / duplicate ACKs for 30 minutes.
6) If issues persist, rollback: restore previous conntrack timeout and port-range, disable MSS clamp, and revert SNAT config.

Monitoring hooks:
- Synthetic success rate metric: medica.rpc_success_rate
- Netflow ephemeral_ports_highwat alert
- Packet capture pre/post-change (we'll keep 15-minute rolling pcaps)

Risks: brief connection resets for established connections during node-by-node changes; monitoring will be our rollback trigger.

CI/CD / tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-1248

Please ack and I'll schedule the Ops runbook with MedicaHealth.

- Michael
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
